note: Trigger function that keeps the new bigint column equal to customer_id on every insert/update. Touches no table lock.

Add nullable customer_id_new bigint (metadata-only), a NOT VALID 'IS NOT NULL' check (enforced for new rows only) and the sync trigger, all in one short transaction. Locks are taken with a 200 ms lock_timeout and retried, so app queries never queue behind us for longer than that.
Backfill ids [0, 2.5M) in 50k-row batches, one commit per batch (rows are never touched by the app, so no contention).
Vacuum so the dead row versions' space is reused by the next batches instead of growing the table.
Backfill ids from 7.5M to the current max id. Rows inserted since the trigger exists are already filled; the IS NULL filter skips them.
Safety check: stop the plan here if any row is unfilled or differs from customer_id.
Validate the NOT NULL check. Takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE: app reads and inserts keep running during the scan.

The swap, in one short transaction under a 200 ms lock_timeout with retries: SET NOT NULL (no scan: proven by the validated check), drop the check, trigger and old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id. Everything is metadata-only, so the exclusive lock is held for milliseconds. The app keeps using the column name customer_id, so no redeploy is needed.
Drop the now-unused trigger function and refresh statistics for the renamed column.
Final check: customer_id is bigint NOT NULL; fail the plan otherwise.
